title: Noise mitigation around Tampines Expressway and Loyang Flyover works
asked: Dr Charlene Chen asked what interim noise mitigation measures are in place near the Tampines Expressway and Loyang Flyover construction sites, how post-completion noise impact is assessed, and whether extra safeguards will protect residents' sleep, health and children's learning in the meantime.
response: Mr Baey Yam Keng listed the interim measures already in place: temporary noise barriers, enclosures around machinery, rubber materials for hammering works, scheduling noisier works during the day, and noise meters to keep levels within National Environment Agency limits. After construction, permanent noise barriers will be erected along the section of Loyang Viaduct facing residential blocks, and a low noise pavement mix will be used for the road surface. In reply to the supplementary, he said the ministry will plan and look for ways to reduce noise impact, weighing cost, technical feasibility and measurable measures, and will work with other agencies to add measures where infrastructure-level mitigation is not adequate.

key_points.point: Interim measures include temporary noise barriers, machinery enclosures, rubber materials for hammering and doing noisier works during the day
key_points.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
key_points.quote: These include temporary noise barriers, enclosures around machinery, the use of special tools such as rubber materials for hammering works, as well as carrying out noisier works as far as possible during the day.

key_points.point: Noise meters are installed to keep levels within National Environment Agency limits
key_points.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
key_points.quote: Noise meters are also installed to ensure that noise levels do not exceed the levels stipulated by the National Environment Agency (NEA).

key_points.point: Permanent noise barriers will be erected after construction along the Loyang Viaduct section facing residential blocks
key_points.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
key_points.quote: Post-construction, permanent noise barriers will be erected along the section of Loyang Viaduct facing residential blocks.

key_points.point: A low noise pavement mix will be used for the road surface
key_points.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
key_points.quote: Low noise pavement mix that better absorb noise will also be used for the road surface.

key_points.point: The ministry will plan and look for ways to reduce noise impact on residents near road infrastructure
key_points.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
key_points.quote: We will plan and look for ways to reduce noise, noise impact on residents living near road infrastructure.

key_points.point: Decisions weigh cost, technical feasibility and measurable measures, since noise tolerance differs between people
key_points.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
key_points.quote: it is about taking a balance of cost, about technical feasibilities and also using very measurable tangible measures because residents' noise tolerance levels could differ from person to person

key_points.point: Where infrastructure-level mitigation is not adequate, the ministry will work with other agencies to add measures
key_points.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
key_points.quote: When infrastructure-level kind of mitigation are not adequate, we will definitely look at possible ways, working with other agencies to see how we can add on to the measures to reduce the impact on residents living around it.

key_points.point: There is a schedule of resurfacing expressways with noise reducing pavement mix, especially near residential areas
key_points.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
key_points.quote: As for noise reducing pavement mix, we have a schedule of resurfacing these expressways, especially near residential areas.

key_points.point: The new section being built near the residents will already use the noise-reducing mix for the road surface
key_points.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
key_points.quote: But this new section that we are building near Dr Chan's residents will already be using the noise-reducing mix for the road surface.

left_open: Whether post-completion monitoring will take place and what additional mitigation would follow if noise levels exceed what residents can reasonably live with
Whether enhanced soundproofing such as improved window treatments or insulation will be explored
How residents' well-being is weighed when new highways and road expansions are planned
supplementary: Whether noise-reducing road surfaces can be expedited, post-completion noise monitoring added, and extra soundproofing such as window insulation explored.
